text:
alice: Heads-up — we started seeing a sustained p99 jump for eu-west requests after the kernel selector rollout. p50 roughly same, throughput constant, p99 went from ~420ms to ~1.9s. Noting this during the canary that enabled 'auto-kernel-swap'.
ben_perf: Can you paste the raw profiling snippets and routing breakdown? Might be microbatching + kernel combo.
alice: Pasting a short snippet from the profiler and traffic breakdown:
```
model: opt-2.7b
seq_len: 512
microbatch tested: [1,2,4,8]
KV_cache_hit_rate: 0.72 overall (eu-west)
--- perf (local GPU only) ---
microbatch=1: p50=150ms p95=420ms p99=520ms
microbatch=2: p50=170ms p95=500ms p99=900ms
microbatch=4: p50=210ms p95=800ms p99=1.9s
microbatch=8: p50=350ms p95=1.2s p99=3.4s
kernel_selector: preferred_kernel=matmul_tiled_v2
fallback_kernel=matmul_generic (used for some shards)
notes: when fallback_kernel used, attention path switched to slower attn_v1 (no fused softmax)
```
ben_perf: That pattern screams kernel alignment + batching boundary. v2 kernel requires certain tile alignment; at microbatch=4 we slip into a slow codepath. Also check whether cross-region fallbacks are inflating p99 (network + cold KV).
carla_sre: @alice how many requests got routed cross-region during the spike? We had a temporary eu capacity blip and routing allowed fallback to us-west. Even a small percent can blow up p99 for the aggregated metric.
alice: Traffic snapshot: eu-west steady QPS 420; 9% of requests fell back to us-west over 12 minutes while autoscale spun up. Cross-region RTT added ~320ms median, but tail network jitter + cold KV miss amplified to +1.1s on p99 for those requests.
dmitri: Relevant routing snippet from the test cluster (sanitized):
```yaml
routing_policy: latency_first
fallback:
  enable_cross_region: true
  max_pct: 10
  fallback_threshold_ms: 800
  prefer_local_cache: false  # oops, this was false in canary
```
carla_sre: Ah — prefer_local_cache=false explains extra KV misses. If a request goes to us-west it can't read eu cache entries, so hit-rate drops and each token generation pays cache rebuild cost. That + the slower kernel path = compound tail.
ben_perf: Two prio action items: (1) force kernel override to 'matmul_tiled_v1' for opt-2.7b in eu until we get alignment fix, (2) disable cross-region fallback for that canary or set prefer_local_cache=true. Also run a focused microbenchmark across microbatch sizes with kernel selection logging.
perf-bot: ALERT: p99 > SLA threshold for eu-west (1.9s) detected at 2026-02-11T08:23:11Z. Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/p99-investigation
infra-bot: Deploy completed: autoscaler-rule-tuning (#3321) — rolled back for eu-west canary as requested.
alice: Quick experiment results after disabling cross-region fallback and pinning kernel:
```
post-change: microbatch=4: p99 drops to 560ms (was 1.9s). overall p99 back to ~480ms at steady QPS.
notes: KV_hit_rate improved to 0.86 after prefer_local_cache=true.
```
carla_sre: Nice. Longer-term we should: 1) teach routing to prefer local-cache affinity before cross-region, 2) make kernel selector aware of microbatch propagation (avoid tile-mismatch), 3) add per-route p99 that excludes cross-region fallbacks for SLOs.
ben_perf: Agreed. I'll open tickets: PERF-1243 (kernel alignment test suite + selector heuristics), PERF-1244 (microbatching policy defaults), ROUTE-981 (cache affinity in routing).
dmitri: I'll schedule a canary that forces local-only routing and runs microbatch sweep during 03:00 maintenance window.
alice: Thanks — lowering blast radius for next rollout. :thumbsup:
